To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. Seller material treated as untrusted counterparty drafting.

## Preliminary: framing in the Seller package to disregard

The Seller's cover material tries to narrow our review. None of it binds us or changes the playbook.

- **"[STANDARD] … reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny"**: These labels are the Seller's own. Nothing in our record shows the buyer agreed to them. Every issue in the package touches a playbook position, so all are reviewed below.
- **"Settled at principal level … FINAL and not intended to be re-opened"**: We have no record of buyer agreement. In particular, Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback. Treat this as a negotiating assertion.
- **"Market context" (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge bars)**: These are Seller advocacy, not a benchmark we have adopted. Our playbook governs.
- **"The parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package"**: There is no evidence of this. Both are rejected below.

The Disclosure Letter is factually candid in several places (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, title). Those admissions support our positions and are cited below.

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% fallback is not unlocked, and the Seller's "agreed at principal level" claim does not substitute for Amelia Frost's written authority.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000. Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket.** The Seller's figures are 5x our position on both thresholds, and the deductible structure further erodes recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. Also proposes that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** The fallback is not authorised, and the default wording would silently pull Title, Tax, IP and fraud claims into the general time bar (see SPA-N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so capping them at 20% is unacceptable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No express carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," which would by default cover fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express overriding carve-out.** "Any nature" captures fraud, and our playbook does not permit any waiver of this protection.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026 (DL 1.1), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or prudent searches.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2. Limit to the specific disclosures in sections 2–10, each made fairly and with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter.** Whole-data-room and register disclosure would neutralise the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier remains, it should apply only to the Seller's warranties, by reference to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** It combines buyer knowledge with constructive data-room knowledge and would bar claims on matters the Seller itself has flagged.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **DL §2 admits:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30%, of FY26 revenue. No final written consent or evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion condition requiring effective consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 and evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Not consent-on-delivery, and not reasonable endeavours alone.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make effective, unconditional Bluefen consent plus satisfaction evidence a non-waivable-by-Seller condition precedent.** A 30% revenue customer cannot be left to endeavours and paper delivery.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion."
- **DL §3 admits:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, and no discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require payout letter, direct payment to Riverlark in the funds flow and executed releases (including PPSR) as Completion deliverables.** A post-Completion release is not authorised and leaves AUD 3.2m of security over the target. The change-control (cl 8.1) exposure also needs to be closed off.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised.
- **DL §5 confirms:** They are absent from the funds flow, and it is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or otherwise funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require an express line item or Seller funding, plus a specific indemnity covering bonuses and on-costs.** The current funds flow silently excludes them, so the cost would fall on the Company after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate."
- **DL §4 confirms:** Transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, which is not independently verified. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity covering IP ownership, infringement and the costs of securing assignment, while preserving the SOW3 cure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted. Broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 payment cure, and seek a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.** Paying the fee does not by itself cure an ownership gap. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as confirmed either way until it is verified.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material."
- **DL §6 confirms:** About 1,240 records were potentially exposed. Access, scope and the notification position are not established.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation and ongoing updates. We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation. Require pre-Completion covenants on log preservation, investigation (including the notifiable data breach assessment) and regular updates, with an appropriate specific protection.** "Not expected to be material" is unsupported while the investigation is preliminary. Equally, we should not assert a breach.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **DL §8:** Silent on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of DD-008 and DD-011 together. No automatic classification as Debt and no automatic price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label, and do not demand a Debt or price adjustment yet. Investigate the timing, scope, terminability and accrual of the related renewals first.** The facts are undetermined in both directions.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Several provisions combine to fold Title, Tax, IP and fraud into the general regime: the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" default (cl 12.3/13), "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5), title under general caps, and Tax/IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant claims kept as separate categories, with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Draft express category-specific limitation clauses, plus an order-of-precedence clause stating that general limitations do not apply to the other categories unless expressly stated.** The Seller's drafting achieves through defaults what it states openly in SPA-N-004.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- **DL §10 concedes:** DD-012 only identifies the source relied on, and does not reflect any Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as sufficient. Require an ASIC extract, PPSR search, share certificates, Seller board/authority resolutions and encumbrance confirmations, backed by Fundamental Warranties.** An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain open. We assume neither unlimited liability nor any resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** Nothing in our record settles them, and subjecting them to the general cap and time bar would prejudice the outcome.

## Other points noted
- **Lease (DL §7) and Mossvale (DL §9):** The Seller describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not consents triggered by a share sale. We should confirm this by reviewing DD-007 and DD-009 for change-of-control wording rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation.
- **DL 1.4 (no admission):** Acceptable in principle, but it must not dilute the specific disclosures or the indemnities.

## Summary

| Issue | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| 001 Cap | Reject 20%; 25% / AUD 6m (no Frost authority) |
| 002 Thresholds | Reject; AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping basket |
| 003 Time limit | Reject 18m; 24m; delete "all Claims" default |
| 004 Fundamental | Reject; 100% cap, 6+ years, separate regime |
| 005 Fraud | Insert full non-waivable carve-out |
| 006 Disclosure | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 007 Buyer knowledge | Delete cl 8.3 |
| 008 Bluefen | Effective consent + conditions evidence as condition precedent |
| 009 Riverlark | Payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion |
| 010 Bonuses | Line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs |
| 011 Ironquay | Broaden indemnity, keep SOW3 cure |
| 012 DD-006 | Preservation, investigation and update covenants; neutral on breach |
| 013 Sandbar | Investigate; no automatic Debt or deduction |
| 014 Categories | Express separation and precedence |
| 015 Title | Independent evidence required |
| 016 Tax/IP | Remain open |

**Escalation:** No fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) should be offered without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. If the deal team wants to use any of them, that approval should be sought first.

- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted. Broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 payment cure, and seek a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.** Paying the fee does not by itself cure an ownership gap. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as confirmed either way until it is verified.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material."
- **DL §6 confirms:** About 1,240 records were potentially exposed. Access, scope and the notification position are not established.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation and ongoing updates. We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation. Require pre-Completion covenants on log preservation, investigation (including the notifiable data breach assessment) and regular updates, with an appropriate specific protection.** "Not expected to be material" is unsupported while the investigation is preliminary. Equally, we should not assert a breach.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **DL §8:** Silent on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of DD-008 and DD-011 together. No automatic classification as Debt and no automatic price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label, and do not demand a Debt or price adjustment yet. Investigate the timing, scope, terminability and accrual of the related renewals first.** The facts are undetermined in both directions.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Several provisions combine to fold Title, Tax, IP and fraud into the general regime: the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" default (cl 12.3/13), "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5), title under general caps, and Tax/IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/indemnity and covenant claims kept as separate categories, with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Draft express category-specific limitation clauses, plus an order-of-precedence clause stating that general limitations do not apply to the other categories unless expressly stated.** The Seller's drafting achieves through defaults what it states openly in SPA-N-004.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- **DL §10 concedes:** DD-012 only identifies the source relied on, and does not reflect any Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as sufficient. Require an ASIC extract, PPSR search, share certificates, Seller board/authority resolutions and encumbrance confirmations, backed by Fundamental Warranties.** An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain open. We assume neither unlimited liability nor any resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** Nothing in our record settles them, and subjecting them to the general cap and time bar would prejudice the outcome.

## Other points noted
- **Lease (DL §7) and Mossvale (DL §9):** The Seller describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not consents triggered by a share sale. We should confirm this by reviewing DD-007 and DD-009 for change-of-control wording rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation.
- **DL 1.4 (no admission):** Acceptable in principle, but it must not dilute the specific disclosures or the indemnities.
